subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Dunning-Kruger Effect
description: A 60-second lesson on The Dunning-Kruger Effect.

hook.text: A man robs a bank with lemon juice on his face, sure it makes him invisible to cameras. He was arrested quickly.

buildup.text: Dunning and Kruger found that the least competent people overestimate their skill the most.

discovery.text: The problem: the skills needed to be good at something are the same skills needed to judge your ability.

twist.text: Experts make the opposite error—they assume others know what they know and underrate their own skills.

climax.text: The cure is feedback and metacognition. Once beginners learn the skill, they recognize their past errors.

punchline.text: You need skill to know you lack skill.

quiz.question: What drives the Dunning-Kruger effect?
options: Lacking the skills to evaluate one's own competence
